problem: End-to-end ImageNav agents trained from reward alone must implicitly learn wide-baseline visual correspondence between observation and goal image. This is too weak a signal, so prior work relied on panoramic input, Siamese late-fusion encoders, or explicit feature matching in modular pipelines.
motivation: Perception, and goal detection plus relative pose estimation in particular, is a major bottleneck in goal-oriented navigation. ImageNav needs a comparison strategy that is essentially a correspondence problem, yet it is rarely treated as one. Pretext tasks that target correspondence directly should give a strong prior for an end-to-end agent in the mono-view setting.
key_idea: Pre-train a large binocular ViT (cross-attention between observation and goal) first with cross-view completion (CroCo) and then with relative pose and visibility estimation, then combine it with a small monocular ResNet encoder in an RL-trained recurrent policy (DEBiT); correspondence emerges in the cross-attention.
insight: Early fusion via cross-attention only helps when the pre-training signals match it. Trained from reward alone, DEBiT-B gets SR 6.8 and a Siamese ResNet gets 10.1, but with CroCo+RPEV DEBiT-B reaches 83.0. CroCo alone gives about 60-66 SR and RPEV alone gives 12-24, so both stages are needed. Adding RPEV to a Siamese late-fusion encoder, or to a hybrid ResNet+tiny cross-attention, brings no gain, and cross-attention maps show correspondence emerging without explicit supervision.
method: Dual encoder DEBiT: a binocular ViT encoder-decoder b(x_t, x*) for goal detection and pose (skill S3), plus a half-width ResNet-18 monocular encoder m(x_t) trained from scratch for navigable space, obstacles and semantics (S1, S2)
Binocular model: a Siamese ViT encoder E on each image and a cross-attention decoder D (CroCo architecture, DEBiT-L/B/S/T sizes), followed by a projection g to a 3136-dim embedding
Stage 1, CroCo cross-view completion: masked-patch reconstruction of one view from another, pre-trained on 1.8M Habitat image pairs

Stage 2, RPEV finetuning: heads predict translation t, rotation R (Procrustes-normalized) and visibility v with an L1 loss; pose loss is gated by visibility > tau. Trained on a new dataset of about 68.8M pairs from Gibson/MP3D/HM3D sampled along shortest paths at 5 distance bands

Stage 3, RL: GRU policy plus monocular encoder trained with PPO (reward 10*success - geodesic increase - 0.01); b is frozen (only g tuned) or frozen with AdaptFormer adapters trained by RL; the RPEV head is discarded
Modular proof of concept: Active Neural SLAM plus binocular encoder b, switching between goal navigation and exploration by thresholding the predicted visibility

setting.backbone: DEBiT: CroCo-style binocular ViT (pre-trained, frozen, optionally with adapters) + half-width ResNet-18 (from scratch) + GRU policy trained with PPO
setting.model_size: DEBiT-L binocular 120M (plus small monocular ResNet); B 55M, S 24M, T 17M
setting.training_data: CroCo pre-training on 1.8M Habitat image pairs; RPEV on about 68.8M pairs from Gibson/MP3D/HM3D; RL for 200M steps (Instance-ImageNav: 100M ImageNav then 100M Instance-ImageNav)
setting.action_space: low-level: MOVE FORWARD 0.25m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 10°, STOP (plus LOOK UP/DOWN for Instance-ImageNav)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT poses and visibility used only for pretext training)

numbers.eval_set_note: 14 Gibson-val scenes, episodes from Mezghani et al.

numbers.extra: 200M steps (100M ImageNav + 100M Instance-ImageNav); max over last 5 checkpoints; avg SR 59.3, SPL 32.4

numbers_note: Instance-ImageNav is reported on the val split (max/avg over last 5 checkpoints), not test.
results: DEBiT-L with adapters reaches 94.0 SR / 71.7 SPL on ImageNav (Gibson val, mono-view), beating OVRL-v2 (82.0/58.7) and VC1-ViT-L (81.6 SR) with 200M rather than 500M steps. On Instance-ImageNav it gets 61.1 SR / 33.5 SPL, beating the feature-matching SOTA of Krantz et al. (56.1/23.3).
limitations: Pretext tasks are done in equal-intrinsics ImageNav settings, so Instance-ImageNav needs adapters, and the model without them fails
Requires large-scale pre-training data and a large ViT; the modular integration underperforms end-to-end
Evaluated only in simulation on Gibson/Instance-ImageNav val, with no real-robot experiments
compares_to: Siamese hwRN18 (Zhu et al./Mezghani et al.)
